apps.name: Ram Checker
apps.subtitle: Check for your ram in iPhone
apps.localizedDescription:
RAM Checker:

A lightweight iOS utility that shows what your device — and the app itself — actually has access to at the kernel level: physical RAM, per-app memory budget, and the live status of Apple's memory-related entitlements.

Built for sideloading via LiveContainer / SideStore / similar tools, since the entitlements it checks (increased-memory-limit, extended-virtual-addressing) require a real Apple Developer signature to actually be granted by the kernel.

Features:

• Device card — model name (mapped from the raw hardware identifier) and current iOS version.
• Memory card — physical RAM, per-app memory budget (os_proc_available_memory), current footprint (phys_footprint), and remaining headroom.
• Entitlement status card — reads the live kernel-granted state of:.

• com.apple.developer.kernel.increased-memory-limit.
• com.apple.developer.kernel.extended-virtual-addressing.

Kryptos is an iPhone and Android app that encrypts conversations inside any messenger.

You type the message straight into WhatsApp, Telegram or an SMS, tap the padlock on the Kryptos keyboard, and the field holds ciphertext instead of your text. On the other end it works the other way round: on Android Kryptos decrypts the text on screen without leaving the messenger, on iPhone it shows the text above the keyboard once the ciphertext is copied. The messenger, the carrier and anyone who intercepts the message on the way see a run of characters they cannot read.

The app is the same on both systems and uses one format, so it does not matter which phone your contact carries.

versions.localizedDescription:
What is new:

• Chinese: the interface and a keyboard layout with pinyin input.
• Profanity, insults and potentially dangerous words are out of all three text steganography modes, in English, Russian and German. 197 words were replaced with neutral ones, so each language still holds 4,096 words.
• Keyboard: the Paste and Clear buttons are bigger and sit in one row, the message field size is adjustable, and the Kryptos badge can be hidden.
• Send after encrypting now works in messengers that send with their own button. It needs the on-screen decryption service, which Android switches off on update.
• Profiles and contacts can be renamed, a long press on a message opens a menu with copy and delete, and a deleted message is wiped completely.
• A profile with unreadable storage no longer takes the app down: it opens on a working profile and names the one that is unavailable.

Fixes:

Around twenty, among them: send after encrypting did not send in messengers with their own button, the keyboard closed after sending, switching to a profile with damaged storage closed the app and left it on the erase-everything screen, the app could create a key over existing data and make it unreadable, the password stayed in memory after the key was derived, hiding a message in a photo used 80 MB more memory than needed.

Breaking change. Covers made by the ordinary-words and smart-sentences steganography modes cannot be read by versions before 2.3.2. Both sides have to update.

• Китайский язык: интерфейс и раскладка клавиатуры с вводом по пиньиню.
• Из всех трёх режимов текстовой стеганографии убраны матерные, оскорбительные и потенциально опасные слова на английском, русском и немецком. 197 слов заменены нейтральными, объём остался 4096 слов на язык.

Около двадцати, среди них: отправка после шифрования не работала в мессенджерах со своей кнопкой, клавиатура закрывалась после отправки, переключение на профиль с повреждённым хранилищем закрывало приложение и оставляло его на экране полного стирания, приложение могло создать ключ поверх существующих данных и сделать их нечитаемыми, пароль оставался в памяти после вычисления ключа, скрытие сообщения в фото занимало на 80 МБ больше памяти, чем нужно.

versions.localizedDescription:
0.3.14 Beta 15 - playback reliability wave (never-recovers stall, dead-source hop, watch history, Dolby Vision colour):

A focused reliability release. Install this over any earlier build. This build comes out of a full audit of a real diagnostic log and fixes the most severe playback failures behind it: streams that spun forever and never recovered, sources that took half a minute to give up, watch-history marks that did not show, and an unsafe Dolby Vision colour fallback. It builds clean on every Apple target; several of these are behavioural fixes best confirmed on your own hardware, so please test and share logs.

What's fixed:

Playback no longer spins forever and never recovers. A stream that froze mid-play while the picture still read as buffering could sit on a spinner indefinitely: the Apple TV recovery watchdog treated that buffering state as normal and never stepped in, even though the same freeze on iPhone and Mac already recovered. The watchdog now observes through a buffering freeze (the shared mid-play stall policy the touch players already use): a genuine wait keeps its full patience, but a stuck stream is recovered on its own instead of stranding you. Apple TV.

Marking something watched shows up right away. Marking a movie or episode watched from its detail page could leave the checkmark on its old value even though the mark was recorded, because the page only refreshed when a few specific fields changed and the watched flag was not one of them. It now refreshes on the watched change itself. Apple TV, iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

A dead source is dropped in a couple of seconds, not half a minute. A source that opens but delivers no actual video (an empty, truncated, or expired link) was handed to the backup player, which also got nothing, wasting about thirty seconds. Such a source is now recognised as genuinely dead from its very first failed read and the app jumps straight to your next source. Apple TV, iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Rewinding keeps working on long streams. The stream can build minutes of video ahead of where you are watching, and that lead used to eat into the window kept behind you, so a rewind a little way back could be refused as out of range. The producer now paces itself, pausing when it runs far ahead, so it never collapses your rewind history. Apple TV, iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Dolby Vision fallback no longer risks the wrong colours. When a Dolby Vision title has to fall back to the plain player, the app used to force a Dolby Vision colour space purely because the title was labelled Dolby Vision, which is not safe for every Dolby Vision variant and could tint the picture. It now applies that only when the format's own signalling proves it is HDR10 compatible, protects the incompatible variant, and otherwise waits for real decoded colour information before deciding. Apple TV, iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Seeking no longer visibly jumps backward before it starts. A seek lands on the nearest earlier keyframe for decoder correctness, and that earlier point (up to about two seconds before where you asked) used to be shown before catching up. The player now decodes from the keyframe silently and only reveals the picture at the point you actually requested. Apple TV, iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Fewer dropped frames, and a provider that is down is not hammered. Frame-drop measurement no longer counts the transient drops around a display-mode switch, a fresh render start, or a seek, and thumbnail capture is kept off the picture's critical path; and a source provider that is failing (for example a debrid service having a bad moment) now gets a single probe after a cooldown instead of being retried on every screen refresh. Apple TV, iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Known issues, please read:

• Watch history beyond the marker still wants a real-device check. The detail-page marker fix is in and confirmed; a full round trip of a live watch tick updating your resume point and the title appearing in Continue Watching was traced as intact but could not be verified end to end without hardware. If a real play does not show up in Continue Watching, please share a diagnostic.
• Dropped frames on 4K Dolby Vision are measured more honestly and the worst bursts are avoided, but the underlying presentation-path cause is not fully cured.
• Trakt sign-in now works again (the OAuth broker went live between betas), no app update needed.

Please test:

• A long play on Apple TV: watch 20+ minutes of a heavy 4K stream; if it ever freezes on a spinner it should now recover on its own. Share the diagnostics log (Settings > Diagnostics) after any failure.
• Mark a movie or episode watched from its detail page and confirm the checkmark moves immediately; then play something, exit, and confirm it appears in Continue Watching.
• A source that will not play: confirm it moves on within a couple of seconds instead of a long reconnect.
• Rewind a good way back during a long stream; it should not be refused.
• Dolby Vision on capable hardware: confirm true DV, and no colour tint if a title falls back to the plain player.

Android:

Android is not attached to this build. It is roughly 45% of the way to the Apple apps, with about 55% remaining: the spine (accounts, sync, debrid, phone and TV shells, playback engines, downloads, IPTV, torrent serving, source ranking, Picture-in-Picture, MediaSession) is in, and what remains is feature breadth against the parity plan, real on-device playback proof, a stable signing identity, and signed-install verification. Full parity stays the target; a preview APK returns in a later build.

Applesauce:

A playful emulator for iOS. It plays supported 32-bit iPhone games on modern iPhones — no jailbreak required, though JIT is. It installs and runs on iPadOS too, but every game runs as an iPhone guest for now: the core's iPad device families are not yet reachable from the app.

The emulation is entirely the work of touchHLE and its fork HyperHLE; this project is the iOS app built around them — the interface, the build system and the packaging. Neither project is connected to Applesauce or endorses it, so please report problems here rather than to them. No games or Apple software are included.

versions.localizedDescription:
Applesauce 0.4.0:

This release renames the app. What was touchHLE for iOS is now Applesauce — a playful emulator for iOS. The name, icon and identifier are new; the emulation is the same as 0.3.0, plus the fixes below.

Applesauce is an unaffiliated fork. The emulation is entirely the work of touchHLE and its fork HyperHLE, and neither project is connected to this one or endorses it. Please report problems here rather than to them.

Read this first: your games do not move automatically:

The bundle identifier changed, so Applesauce installs alongside the old app with an empty library rather than replacing it.

• Open Files and go to On My iPhone.
• Find the old app's folder — HyperHLE if you had 0.2.0 or 0.3.0, touchHLE if you had 0.1.0.
• Move touchHLE_apps from it into the Applesauce folder. Move touchHLE_sandbox too if you want your saves.
• Delete the old app.

App-wide settings do not come across; set them again under Settings.

The deployment target drops from 17.4 to 15.0, and there are now three IPAs:

The TrollStore builds carry the memory entitlements that let older hardware map the emulator's 4GiB guest address space. A free Apple account cannot sign those, which is why this is a TrollStore route rather than a sideloading one.

The permanent-JIT build crashes on launch on A12 and newer (iPhone XS/XR onwards) — iOS 15 bans the entitlement it carries. Use the ordinary TrollStore build there.

iOS 15 and 16 are untested by this project. The support is back-ported from nerivalaitis' work, tested by them on iOS 15. Reports from those versions are the most useful thing you can send.

Fixes:

• A game no longer dies when a rotation is refused. A guest asking to rotate while the host UI still has the old orientation pinned used to panic and take the whole game down mid-play; it now logs a warning and carries on.
• Black screen after rotating, on games without a fullscreen layer. SDL recreates its framebuffer object when the window leaves and re-enters fullscreen, and compositing kept using the one cached at startup.
• A crash inside the emulator no longer wedges the app. Panics were unwinding across the FFI boundary, leaving a black screen and a dead exit button with nothing in the log; they are now caught and reported.
• Guest memory allocation falls back instead of failing outright when iOS refuses the full read-write mapping, which is what blocked older devices.
• JIT detection understands permanent JIT. A TrollStore install with dynamic-codesigning was previously told it had no JIT, and had to use "Start Anyway" every time.
• Portrait is selectable under Settings → Starting Orientation, for games that declare landscape but draw portrait anyway.
• The previous run's log is kept as touchhle-host-previous.log, so force-quitting a hung game no longer destroys the log that recorded the hang.

Both emulator cores carry these fixes.

Credits:

• touchHLE — the original emulator.as the default core.
• nerivalaitis — the iOS 15 back-port, TrollStore packaging and the memory-allocation fallback.

apps.subtitle: Official Website
apps.localizedDescription:
Hotline Navigator:

Official Website.

What the hell is Hotline?:

Hotline in concept, was to replicate a BBS but for the internet age. Modern users would recongize more as a proto peer-to-peer or a Discord like application.

Hotline's Navigator's website has a deeper drive the history of Hotline.

Platform Support:

Right now the iOS, iPadOS, and Android versions are not in their respective app stores and must be built manually or sideloaded.

This is a Tauri-based Hotline client that provides a modern, cross-platform experience for the classic Hotline protocol. Built with React and Rust, it offers:

• Cross-Platform: Single codebase for macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS, iPadOS, and Android.
• Modern Stack: React + TypeScript frontend, Rust backend.

• Native Performance: Tauri's lightweight architecture for fast, efficient apps.

versions.localizedDescription:
v0.2.8:

There's been a lot of rapid changes in Navigator's capabilities so this release UX quality-of-life series of fixes since the Discord style chat introduced a new UX paradigm which inevitable had some loose ends.

Disconnects are detected in seconds instead of minutes, chat icons no longer fall back to gray letter placeholders for emotes or for users who chatted before their info loaded, and! / / commands now appear above the bot's response instead of below it. News browsing also works on multi-tier servers like VesperNet, where top-level entries are folders of folders.

Next release will be new feature bound.

Bugfixes and Improvements:

• Faster disconnect detection — When a server vanishes silently (peer crash, network drop, NAT timeout), the client now notices in ~60s on macOS/Linux and ~130s on Windows, down from the OS TCP retransmit default of 15+ minutes. Auto-reconnect kicks in correspondingly faster.

• News browsing on nested servers — On servers like VesperNet where the top-level news entries are folders containing more folders, navigation no longer dead-ends with an empty article pane. The client now dispatches based on the clicked item's actual type (bundle vs. category) rather than assuming any non-root path holds articles.

Technical:

• TCP SO_KEEPALIVE configured on the control channel via socket2: idle=30s, interval=10s, retries=3 on macOS/Linux. Windows uses the OS default retry count.
• App-level keepalive failure now emits StatusChanged(Disconnected) and clears the transport, instead of silently breaking.

• Optimistic insert tagged with pending: true and optimisticKey; echo dedup matches by userName + message text within a 10s window. /me and /em are preformatted as *** name action to match the server echo. 30s safety timeout clears the pending flag if no echo arrives.
• News load effect dispatches on a tracked newsLeafType (2 = bundle → get_news_categories; 3 = category → get_news_articles). Going back always sets leaf type to bundle, since non-leaf path segments are bundles by invariant.

Installation:

Download the installer for your platform from the release assets.

.dmg = macOS, .msi/.exe = Windows, .apk = Android, .ipa = iOS/iPadOS, Linux hippies can figure it out.

Please note I am not affililated with the Surge Synth Team in any way. Surge XT's GPLv3 licensing prohibits distribution in any kind of App Store or Google Play Store.

The main work done to make this functional:

• Add iOS/Android handling to the cmake system and incompatible libraries (luajit).
• Handle factory presets bundling and APK zip extraction for Android.
• Handle persistent storage of user settings and patches to mobile app data paths.

Surge XT's GPLv3 licensing prohibits distribution in any kind of App Store, so sideloading methods like Sidestore and Alt Store (and all their inconveniences) are the only way to install it to your device. I am not a legal expert but I am not interested in distribution.

The main work done to make this functional:

• Add platform handling to the cmake system and incompatible libraries (luajit).
• Handle factory presets bundling with the app.
• Handle persistent storage of user settings and patches to "On My iPhone > Surge XT".
• Expose JUCE audio "Options" button to iOS/Android UI layer.

Beyond that, there were some quality of life enhancements:

• Allow right-click via two-finger click (tap + hold on the control, then tap with a second finger).
• Allow sub menu access: Surge > Menu > sub-menus can be opened by tap + hold + drag.
• Force landscape mode, handle proper zooming to fit screen.
• Implement touch scrolling, zoom -/+, and "fit to screen" to cram the extensive UI in smaller screens (iPad is usable best-fit, iPhone needs scrolling).

• Keep screen on while app is running.

I find that Surge runs excellently on even my 2018 iPad 6th generation. The basic functionality is there to do what I need to do with Surge: play the synth, control it with a physical MPE MIDI controller, adjust parameters, add effects, and load/import patches (just airdrop them into "On My iPhone > Surge XT > Surge Synth Team > Surge XT > Patches"). However, Surge's feature set is huge and there are probably a lot of corner cases and potential bugs I'm not considering.

Synkplay is available on Apple store and Google Play store.

Changes:

• Fixed file privacy modes breaking sync checks with PC users: hashed filenames now match the desktop client's logic.
• Fixed false "file mismatch" warnings: comparison is now case-insensitive, cross-checks raw against hashed names, and tolerates duration differences under 2.5 seconds.

• Fixed a disconnect loop in large rooms caused by a too-small inbound message buffer.
• Fixed a crash when TLS negotiation fails; a bad server certificate now shows a connection failure and retries.
• Fixed a native thread leak on every reconnect attempt (Android).
• Fixed memory leaks on iOS when leaving a room: all three player engines now fully shut down their position trackers on exit.
• Removed an artificial 100 ms per-message delay on the Ktor network engine that lagged room joins and skewed latency measurement.

• Shared playlist size limits (250 items / 10,000 characters) are now enforced with an upfront warning, matching the official server; the built-in server enforces the same on incoming playlists.
• Controllers can now set other users' readiness across clients: the setOthersReadiness capability is advertised both ways, and "X was set as ready by Y" is announced in the room.
• Users switching rooms now appear and disappear from the user list immediately instead of lingering for up to 15 seconds.
• Server error messages (such as "Wrong password supplied") are now shown in the room instead of failing silently into an endless reconnect loop.
• Trusted domains now match the desktop client exactly: exact host, www variant, *.wildcards, and path prefixes; arbitrary subdomains are no longer trusted implicitly.

• Fixed a possible crash when leaving a room while the player engine fails to shut down.
• mpv on iOS no longer auto-plays right after loading media; it now waits for the room or the user to unpause, matching Android.

Translations:

Translations are now live on Weblate — you can contribute by visiting the hosted Weblate project to translate existing strings or add a new language entirely. Contributions are very welcome since I do add and edit strings fairly regularly and it's easy for some languages to fall behind.

The app is on Google Play, but releases there may be delayed by review times. Downloading the APK directly from here ensures you get the latest version.

Use universal if you're unsure which APK to pick. Most modern phones should use arm64-v8a; if that doesn't work, try armeabi-v7a. x86_64 and x86 builds are available too.

If you don't need multi-engine support, syncplay-version-exo-only.apk is the smallest option. Otherwise, I recommend the full APK for mpv/VLC support (more potent video player engines).

apps.localizedDescription:
Tesstats:

A beautiful, read‑only stats app for your Tesla — powered by your own TeslaMate server. For iPhone, iPad and Mac.

Tesstats shows your car's live status, trips, charging sessions, battery health and rich analytics — at a glance, in a clean dark interface. It never sends any command to your car: it only reads the data TeslaMate already collects.

versions.localizedDescription:
Rearrangeable screens, tappable units, tariff plans — and the app is finally translated end to end.

Every screen is yours to arrange:

Summary, Trips, Charging, Battery and Stats are built from blocks you can reorder or hide, from the ▦ button on the screen itself or from Settings. Defaults now lead with what most people open the app for — how the car is, and what it cost — with the enthusiast blocks further down.

Tap to change units:

Consumption switches between Wh/km and kWh/100 km, and tyre pressure between bar and psi, by tapping any value. Every value switches together and the choice is remembered.

Tariff plans:

Name a plan, give it price bands, and charging sessions TeslaMate did not cost are priced by when they happened. You set only when each band starts — the day closes itself, so the bands always add up to 24 h. Existing time-of-use setups are migrated automatically. Per-location prices can now be set from a charging session itself, which also explains where its cost came from.

The app follows the language you pick:

179 strings had never been added to the catalogue and always showed in English. Beyond that, dates, weekday names and chart axis labels are formatted from a locale rather than the string table, so a Battery chart could read sáb / lun / mié inside an otherwise English screen. Both are fixed, in both directions.

It stops stalling:

Every scrollable screen re-derived all of its analytics on each redraw. On a three-year history, one pass through Stats measured just over a second of blocked main thread — and the live feed triggers several a second. Screens now recompute only when something actually changed, and Stats does it off the main thread. The worst offender, the phantom-drain estimate, went from 948 ms to 4 ms. The launch splash no longer sits for a second and a half before showing anything.

Maps follow the car:

Drive somewhere new and the map stayed framed on the previous place with the marker off-screen. All four maps now re-aim: the live location, the history map after a filter change, and a trip's route once its real GPS trace arrives.

Smaller fixes:

• The trip row no longer breaks prices across two lines or truncates the efficiency label.
• A tariff plan could never be opened — the selection circle was swallowing the row's tap.
• The settings tabs and the gear button had no VoiceOver name.

Sideload the attached Tesstats.ipa with AltStore. The watch app is stripped from the IPA because AltStore cannot provision it.
